paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.German: This line plot illustrates the relationship between rank and trace values for the COPA dataset, as indicated by the title "Traces $\times 10^{-5}$ (COPA)". The x-axis is labeled "Rank" and employs a logarithmic scale, featuring explicitly labeled tick marks at the values 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, representing the trace values scaled by a factor of $10^{-5}$, uses a linear scale starting at 0.0 with numeric tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.5 up to 1.0. The data is represented by a single solid black line connecting large orange square markers, with vertical black capped error bars extending from each marker. The line begins at a rank of 4 with a y-value of approximately 0.3. It exhibits a slight decline to its lowest point of approximately 0.28 at a rank of 16, before rising sharply to a value of approximately 0.65 at a rank of 64. The upward trend continues at a more gradual slope, concluding at the maximum rank of 256 with a peak y-value of approximately 0.75.
